newsitem.title: GUAM: Guam governor says more than 200 died in crash.
newsitem.headline: Guam governor says more than 200 died in crash.

text.p: More than 200 people died in the crash of Korean Air Lines flight 801, Guam's Governor Carl Gutierrez said on Wednesday.

The governor, who was one of the people at the scene of the crash in a jungle area near Guam's international airport, said only 32 people have been rescued so far but he hoped that rescue workers could find a few more poople alive.
"More than 200 people died," the governor said as he gave the first official death toll of the crash of the Boeing 747 with 254 people on board, many of them Korean honeymooners and tourists.

Gutierrez described the crash scene as eerie. "I heard screams from every corner of the darkness," he said as he described personally rescuing about five people, including an 11-year-old Japanese girl but failing to save her mother.
"You couldn't just stand there and allow the screams to go on without doing what you had to do," he told a news conference.

He said the plane burst into flames after hitting an oil pipeline that runs through the rugged jungle area that islanders call the "boondocks" just outside of the capital. Most of the dead came from the plane's mid-section which was totally consumed by the flames, he said.
